cases.confidence_note: The finding that construction started before compensation is the Bank's own, recorded in its completion report as a mid-term review finding and repeated in the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report. The farm, structure and stone cracker counts, the diversions and the cut-off dates come from the Volta River Authority's own resettlement plan and addendum, published by the Bank. The lender and the implementing agency are therefore reporting on their own project and no independent account of this line's land acquisition was found. The completion report says that by 2011 all outstanding compensation had been fully settled, including for the stone crackers, and does not say how long any individual went unpaid, how many people were affected by the works that began before payment, or how many of the 410 condemned structures were lived in. The addendum's cover prints July 2010 in a shifted-glyph font that text extraction renders as nonsense, so its date is on the document and the catalogue date matches it, though the file name says April 2011. The 2004 plan is dated December 2004 in its own running header and February 2005 on its cover, and both are given. The addendum's table of affected houses does not add up: its district rows give 226, 16 and 1 in the column for the original number of affected people and its total row gives 43 for that column, while its columns for properties on the original line and properties affected by diversion, 292 and 118, do sum to the total of 410. The Independent Evaluation Group's review prints no date on its pages; the 7 May 2018 date is the Bank's catalogue field and is likewise unverified at document level. The same report records recurrent cash flow difficulties at the Communaute Electrique du Benin which delayed disbursement of money set aside to compensate people affected by the Ghana-Togo-Benin 330 kV line. That line sits under the second phase and a separate project number, its construction was financed by other lenders, and the report says the Benin component financed by this credit raised no social safeguard issue because it required no land acquisition or resettlement, so that finding is not carried here.

companies: Kurasini Oil Storage Company Limited, formerly MPS Oil (T) Limited
cases.confidence_note: The 43 named affected people at Ukonga, the amounts paid, the Kurasini and Mbagala sequences and the Managing Director's decision to pay for improvements only all come from TANESCO's own amendment to the project's resettlement plan, published by the Bank in January 2014. The 11,070 affected people, the 16 households at Mzinga Creek and the 3 left unpaid come from the Bank's completion report, which reports the findings of a resettlement audit the Bank itself commissioned; the audit report is not in the Bank's document archive: its list of 67 documents for the project holds no resettlement audit, only financial audit reports, and two title searches for one returned none. The lender and the implementing agency are therefore reporting on their own project and no independent account of these wayleaves was found. The amendment gives no totals by type of loss, and none has been worked out from its list here. The amendment also contradicts itself on the line it covers, its introduction describing a line from Factory Zone III (Gongo la Mboto) to Factory Zone II (Kiwalani) and its Ukonga section a line from Factory Zone II (Gongo la Mboto) to Factory Zone III (Kipawa). No document found says what happened to the three families at Kurasini after their land was bought by the oil storage company, whether the three Mbagala landowners were paid, or whether the three Mzinga Creek households finally received the top-up. The resettlement audit concluded that the Bank's resettlement policy had been followed. The Independent Evaluation Group's review prints no date on its pages; the 18 October 2018 date is the Bank's catalogue field for the document and is unverified at document level.
